title: Mendocino and Our “Needle Park” Problem. When a Local Problem Has International Implications. Who Lost The Sheriff? Whose Business Is It?

content_html_sanitized:
Analysis by Richard Cowan 

A new theme – or meme – has developed in the prohibitionist media – that there is a “backlash” against medical marijuana developing in California. CBS introduced it in September of last year in a particularly dishonest segment on 60 Minutes.

See 

Note to 60 Minutes: The News Is Not That There Is Too Much Freedom In L.A., But That There Is Too Little Freedom Everywhere Else. What Is More Important, The Patients Or Prohibition? 

Today, the New York Times carried a story that furthers the prohibitionist propaganda “Marijuana Hotbed Retreats on Medicinal Use 

” about controversies over the huge marijuana industry in California. 

It also further illustrates why I have such contempt for the Times. 

See 

New York Times Editorial Accidentally Tells the Truth: “The War on Drugs Starts Here”. Indeed It Does! And It Must End There. 

Mendocino, Humboldt, and the other Northern California counties where marijuana is widely grown are sparsely populated, and still remarkably isolated by the mountains. 

And the cannabis plant also grows very well there. 

Prohibition has kindly raised the price to extraordinary levels, and being ordinary Americans, the locals are not above making a profit, and the local merchants are not above taking their money. All of this scandalizes the reporters for CBS and the New York Times, who work for free. (Not really, but if they did, they would still be overpaid.) 

Neither of these stories reports that law enforcement in most of California simply refuse to obey Prop 215 (the medical cannabis Compassionate Use Act.) 

See 

Hugely Important California Supreme Court Ruling Ignored by Media. State Officials Must Obey State – Not Federal – Law. 

Neither recognizes that the problems they describe are the result of prohibition and have little to do with medical marijuana, per se. 

In 1986, Zurich designated its Platzspitz park as a haven for hard drug users, a place where they would be tolerated by police and offered sterile needles and medical care. But, by the early 1990s, "Needle Park" had been swamped with junkies from everywhere. 

Crime rose in the area and the park was an eyesore, so Zurich ended the experiment, and then began a more general policy of heroin maintenance.

The point is that creating little islands of tolerance will concentrate the problems of prohibition in one area. This will then be cited by prohibitionists as proof that legalization doesn’t work. 

From 2002, 

If The Best Two Word Explanation for Cannabis Prohibition Is “Bad Journalism,” The Best 3 Word Explanation Is “Quack, Quack, Quack.” -- Wholesale Malpractice In UK As Lambeth Experiment Spreads. 

and also see 

A "Study" Has Begun On the Affects of the Lambeth Experiment On Children: The Answers Are Obvious, And Reassuring, But the Questions Are Really Frightening. 

Consequently, a well-intended but hopelessly flawed program in one city in Switzerland was then exploited globally by the international prohibitionist propaganda machine. Today’s New York Times story was also carried in the International Herald Tribune, and in the Chicago Tribune . 

The story was not “against” medical cannabis, and almost everyone quoted was supposedly in favor of it. But it is just “out of control.” Clearly, maintaining the Drug War is more important than the well-being of the patients, or any American traditions of personal freedom, or the Judeo-Christian concepts of compassion for the sick and dying…

See 

Prohibitionists to Patients: “Drop Dead!” Police, Politicians, and Quacks Put Cannabis Prohibition Ahead of the Sick, Dying and Disabled. “To Jail In An Ambulance.”

and 

Ethical Failure Of Cannabis Prohibition. Tragedy And Farce. Using the Patients To Protect Prohibition. Analysis by Richard Cowan 

I have strongly criticized national organizations that send in “professionals” who push aside the local activists. That has never been NORML’s approach. 

See 

NORML Executive Director Allen St. Pierre’s Speech At the DPA Conference In Long Beach. 

So, how should the broader marijuana reform deal with the media making an international story out of local problems created by the global Drug War? For instance, some of the local activists in Mendocino managed to offend the county sheriff, who had been trying to stay neutral in the battle over the still undecided Measure B. 

See NORML Executive Director Allen St. Pierre’s Speech At the DPA Conference In Long Beach. 

He then announced that he was going to back the initiative. Is this then just a local problem? 

We cannot and should not push aside the local cannabis community, but we need to make clear to both sides that these local “problems” are not really local, and they are not created by the local tolerance, but by the lack of freedom everywhere. 

We all have a stake in what happens in their community. The prohibitionists know that. We need to learn the same lesson fast. 

See 

Cannabis Prohibition Is “Low-Intensity Warfare” Against Social Peace, Individual Freedom and the Rule of Law. Be very afraid... Three Lessons.
